question: Should the v0.1.x compatibility alias document only the released legacy token contract, or should the matching Carapace CSS be released and consumers migrated before these new token names are published?
rationale: The branch is generated from canonical upstream guidance, and choosing between a version-gated compatibility contract and a coordinated package release is an upstream release-policy decision rather than a safe downstream edit.

options.title: Version-gate the upstream guidance
options.body: Keep the legacy alias restricted to tokens actually exported by released `@openclaw/design-system` versions, then regenerate this PR.

options.title: Release and migrate together
options.body: Publish the matching Carapace CSS contract, update consumer dependencies intentionally, and then regenerate the guidance against that release.

options.title: Pause this refresh
options.body: Leave the generated update unmerged until the canonical compatibility contract is decided upstream.

recommendation.title: Version-gate the upstream guidance
recommendation.body: Keep the legacy alias restricted to tokens actually exported by released `@openclaw/design-system` versions, then regenerate this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review already identifies the canonical upstream correction and release-coordination boundary.
